title: A Little Loop of Green
originalStory: I planted a dandelion seed in a little pot, but it stayed tucked in the dirt for days. Then a green loop poked out, with a crumb of soil balanced on top. I turned the pot toward the window so my tiny plant could see the sky.
visualBible:
Mila: human child, age 5, normal human ears, short curly dark-brown hair, brown eyes, mustard-yellow overalls over a white shirt, teal shoes, small child-sized build.
Mama: adult woman, age 34, normal human ears, long black hair in a braid, brown eyes, lavender sweater, navy trousers, white shoes, tall adult-sized build.

pages.text: I planted a dandelion seed in a little pot while Mama sat beside me. I tucked it into the soft brown dirt and whispered, “See you soon.” But for days, the dirt kept its secret.
pages.illustrationScene: Sulu Boya watercolor style, with soft washes and delicate paper texture. Mila gently pats soil in a small terracotta pot on a low planting table while Mama watches warmly. Show no tools or extra characters; the mood is tender and expectant.

pages.text: Each morning, I checked the pot on our low sunroom table. “Maybe it forgot how to grow,” I told Mama. “We can give it time,” she said, settling beside me.
pages.illustrationScene: Sulu Boya watercolor style. In a wide view of a cozy ground-floor sunroom, Mila in mustard-yellow overalls and Mama in a lavender sweater sit close together on a floor cushion beside a low, stable table. Mila studies the small terracotta pot, whose soil is still bare, while Mama listens with a gentle expression. Closed windows admit soft morning light; nothing is placed on a windowsill, and no other characters are visible.

pages.text: Then one morning, a tiny green loop poked out. A crumb of soil balanced on top like a crooked little hat. All those quiet days, my seed had been beginning.
pages.illustrationScene: Sulu Boya watercolor style. An intimate close-up of the small terracotta pot on the low sunroom table shows a newly emerged green dandelion shoot bent into a loop, with one tiny crumb of soil balanced on its top. Soft light from a closed window falls across the textured dirt. No characters are visible; the mood is quiet wonder.

pages.text: I gently turned the pot toward the closed window so my tiny plant could see the sky. “There you are,” I whispered, sitting beside it in the buttery sunshine. There was room for both of us to grow.
